clues.clue: My older brother was a tiller of the ground.
clues.concern: Cain's being older is inferred from birth order (Genesis 4:1-2), not stated outright. On its own, this clue would also fit Seth, whose older brother was Cain; later clues remove the ambiguity.

clues.clue: I was a keeper of sheep.
The LORD had respect unto my offering from the firstlings of my flock.
My brother rose up against me in the field.

notes: Accurate item. Clue 1 alone could fit Seth, since Cain was also Seth's older brother, but clues 2-4 uniquely identify Abel. Consider wording clue 1 as 'I was a keeper of sheep, but my brother was a tiller of the ground' to tie it more closely to Genesis 4:2.

clues.clue: I was the fourth son of Leah.
I said, let us sell our brother rather than kill him.
clues.concern: Paraphrase of 'What profit is it if we slay our brother... Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites'. Reuben also sought to spare Joseph (Genesis 37:21-22), but he proposed casting him into a pit, not selling him, so the clue still points to Judah.

clues.clue: In Egypt I offered to stay as a bondman in place of my youngest brother.
clues.concern: Reuben offered his own two sons as surety for Benjamin (Genesis 42:37), but only Judah offered himself as a bondman in Egypt.

clues.clue: Jacob said the sceptre would not depart from me.

notes: All four clues are accurate and uniquely identify Judah. The explanation correctly quotes Genesis 49:10.

clues.clue: I was an Egyptian handmaid of Sarai.
I fled into the wilderness, and an angel found me by a fountain of water.
I called the LORD who spoke to me, Thou God seest me.
My son was Ishmael.

notes: Every clue is accurate and fits only Hagar. Zilpah and Bilhah were handmaids of Leah and Rachel, and neither was Egyptian. Keturah was Abraham's later wife. The explanation quotes Genesis 16:13 accurately.

clues.clue: I was the brother of Rebekah.
My nephew served me seven years for my younger daughter.
On the wedding night I gave him my older daughter instead.
My daughters were Leah and Rachel.

notes: All clues are accurate and fit only Laban. Bethuel was Rebekah's father, not her brother. Nahor was her grandfather. Jethro's daughters included Zipporah. The explanation matches Genesis 29:25.

clues.clue: My eyes are described as tender.
My father gave me to Jacob in place of my younger sister.
I was the mother of Reuben, Levi and Judah.
clues.concern: The verses also name Simeon (29:33), but the clue is still accurate as a partial list.

clues.clue: My younger sister was Rachel.

notes: The item is accurate. Genesis 29:16 names Leah as the elder and Rachel as the younger. Genesis 29:17 matches the KJV text quoted. None of the distractors fit the clues: Rachel is the younger sister, Bilhah bore Dan and Naphtali, and Dinah is Leah's daughter.

clues.clue: My mother was an Egyptian handmaid.
An angel told my mother my name before I was born.
My name was given because the LORD had heard my mother's affliction.
My father was Abraham, but I was not the son of the promise.
clues.concern: Minor: he was born when his father was still called Abram (Genesis 16:15-16). Genesis 17:19-21 states that the covenant was with Isaac, not Ishmael. The phrase 'son of the promise' reflects Galatians 4:23 ('by promise') and Romans 9:7-9. The clue is acceptable.

notes: The clues are accurate and uniquely fit Ishmael. Isaac's name was given by God to Abraham (Genesis 17:19), not by an angel to his mother. Esau's mother, Rebekah, was not Egyptian, and Lot was not Abraham's son. The explanation matches Genesis 16:11.

clues.clue: I was the youngest son of Jacob.
My mother died as I was born, and she called me Ben-oni.
clues.concern: KJV spells the name 'Benoni' without a hyphen. This is a minor point.

clues.clue: Joseph's silver cup was found in my sack.
My full brother was Joseph.
clues.concern: Genesis 43:29 ('his mother's son') also supports this clue.

notes: The answer Benjamin is correct and every clue is supported by the text. The explanation accurately reflects Genesis 44:12. Genesis 44:2 identifies the cup as Joseph's silver cup.

clues.clue: I took a Babylonish garment, silver and a wedge of gold from Jericho.
I hid them in the earth in the middle of my tent.
Because of my sin, Israel was defeated at Ai.
clues.concern: The defeat is narrated in Joshua 7:4-5 and attributed to the trespass in the accursed thing (Joshua 7:1, 7:11-12). The clue is supported in context.

clues.clue: I was the son of Carmi, of the tribe of Judah.

notes: Accurate item. Gehazi also took silver and garments (2 Kings 5:23-24), but those were from Naaman, not from Jericho. The Jericho, Ai and Carmi details exclude him. All other distractors are clearly excluded.

clues.clue: The prophetess Deborah called me to fight.
I would not go to battle unless Deborah went with me.
I led ten thousand men down from mount Tabor.
I fought against Sisera, captain of Jabin's army.

notes: All clues are accurate to Judges 4 (KJV). Judges 4:4-6 has Deborah, a prophetess, send for Barak. Judges 4:8 has his condition that she go with him. Judges 4:14 says 'Barak went down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.' Judges 4:2 and 4:7 name Sisera as captain of Jabin's army. None of the clues fit Gideon, Joshua or Jephthah. The explanation quotes Judges 4:8 accurately.

clues.clue: I was a judge of Israel from the tribe of Benjamin.
clues.concern: KJV calls Ehud a 'deliverer' and a 'Benjamite'; he is never explicitly titled a 'judge', though he is traditionally counted among the judges. This is minor.

clues.clue: I was left-handed.
I made a dagger with two edges, a cubit long.
I killed Eglon, the king of Moab.

notes: The answer and explanation are accurate, and the ref_kjv text matches Judges 3:15. No distractor fits: Othniel was the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother (Judges 3:9). Shamgar slew Philistines with an ox goad (Judges 3:31). Gideon was a Manassite (Judges 6:15). Optionally, reword 'judge' to 'deliverer' to align with the KJV wording.

clues.clue: I was a Gileadite and a mighty man of valour.
clues.concern: 'Mighty man of valour' is also applied to Gideon (Judges 6:12), but 'Gileadite' makes this clue unique to Jephthah.

clues.clue: My brothers drove me out, and I lived in the land of Tob.
I made a vow to the LORD before fighting the children of Ammon.
My daughter came out to meet me with timbrels and dances.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV. Judges 11:2 says the brothers 'thrust out' Jephthah, and 11:3 says he 'fled from his brethren, and dwelt in the land of Tob', so 'drove me out' is a fair paraphrase. The explanation accurately reflects Judges 11:34. The partial overlap with Gideon on 'mighty man of valour' is resolved by 'Gileadite' and the other clues.

clues.clue: I was Jacob's firstborn son.
I found mandrakes in the field and brought them to my mother.
I persuaded my brothers to cast Joseph into a pit instead of killing him.
clues.concern: Judah also talked the brothers out of killing Joseph (Genesis 37:26-27), but his proposal was to sell him, not cast him into the pit. The pit detail makes this uniquely Reuben.

clues.clue: I planned to rescue Joseph and bring him back to our father.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV. Clue 1 is also supported by Genesis 29:32 and 49:3, and clue 4 by Genesis 37:29-30. The explanation correctly paraphrases Genesis 37:22.

clues.clue: My father was a priest of Midian.
I met my husband when he helped my sisters and me water our flock.
My husband later led Israel out of Egypt.
clues.concern: The verse speaks of the LORD bringing Israel out, though Moses is clearly the human leader throughout (e.g., Exodus 3:10). This is acceptable.

clues.clue: I circumcised my son with a sharp stone.

notes: All clues are supported by Exodus 2:16-21 and Exodus 4:25. In Exodus 2:21, 'the man' is the priest of Midian (Reuel, named in 2:18), so the explanation's paraphrase is accurate. None of the distractors fits: Jochebed's husband was Amram, Miriam is Moses' sister, and Rahab is in Joshua.

clues.clue: I was the son of Jonathan.
I became lame when my nurse fled with me and I fell.
King David restored to me all the land of Saul.
I ate continually at the king's table.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV. Ishbosheth was Saul's son, not Jonathan's. Ziba was Saul's servant: he was told to till the land for Mephibosheth (9:10) and was later given Mephibosheth's land (16:4), but none of the clues fit him. Absalom does not fit any clue. The explanation matches 2 Samuel 9:13.

clues.clue: My husband Elimelech and I moved to Moab during a famine.
clues.concern: Verse 1 calls him 'a certain man of Bethlehemjudah'; his name Elimelech and his wife's name Naomi are given in verse 2.

clues.clue: My husband and both my sons died in Moab.
I asked to be called Mara, because the Almighty had dealt very bitterly with me.
My daughter-in-law Ruth would not leave me.
clues.concern: Ruth 1:14 ('Ruth clave unto her') and 1:18 also support this. Ruth is Orpah's sister-in-law, not her daughter-in-law, so the clue does not fit the distractor Orpah.

notes: All clues are accurate against the KJV and uniquely identify Naomi. Orpah was Naomi's other daughter-in-law, but she was not Elimelech's wife and she returned to her people. Elisabeth and Hannah do not fit any clue. The explanation quotes Ruth 1:20 accurately. Difficulty 1 is appropriate.

clues.clue: I was a Hittite and one of David's mighty men.
clues.concern: The Hittite identification is stated at 2 Samuel 11:3, and the mighty-men listing is at 2 Samuel 23:39 and 1 Chronicles 11:41. The clue is accurate.

clues.clue: I would not go down to my house while the ark and the army stayed in tents.
I carried a letter to Joab that arranged my own death.
My wife was Bathsheba.

notes: All clues are accurate and uniquely fit Uriah. Joab received the letter but did not carry it, so he is not a defensible alternative. The explanation matches 2 Samuel 11:15.

clues.clue: I was the captain of King David's army.
clues.concern: Benaiah also later became captain of the host, though under Solomon (1 Kings 2:35), and Abner was captain of Saul's host, so the clue mainly separates Joab by the qualifier 'King David's'.

clues.clue: My mother was Zeruiah.
clues.concern: Abishai and Asahel were also sons of Zeruiah, but neither is among the options.

clues.clue: I killed Abner at the gate of Hebron.
I thrust three darts through Absalom's heart as he hung in an oak.
clues.concern: Minor wording issue: the verse says Absalom was 'yet alive in the midst of the oak'. The hanging is described in 2 Samuel 18:9-10.

notes: Joab is unambiguously correct. Each clue is supported by the KJV text: 2 Samuel 8:16 / 1 Chronicles 18:15 (captain), 2 Samuel 2:18 / 1 Chronicles 2:16 (son of Zeruiah), 2 Samuel 3:27 (killed Abner in the gate of Hebron), and 2 Samuel 18:14 (three darts through Absalom). The explanation matches the cited verse.

clues.clue: I was the servant of the prophet Elisha.
I told my master that the Shunammite woman had no child.
I ran after Naaman and took silver and garments from him.
clues.concern: Naaman urged him and bound two talents of silver and two changes of garments, so 'took' is a slight simplification. Gehazi did ask for them under a false pretext (v.22), so the clue is acceptable.

clues.clue: The leprosy of Naaman clung to me.

notes: All clues point uniquely to Gehazi. None of the distractors fits: Elisha was the master, Ziba was Saul's servant, and Baruch was Jeremiah's scribe. The explanation accurately reflects 2 Kings 5:27.

clues.clue: I was a servant of Solomon, from the tribe of Ephraim.
clues.concern: KJV calls him 'an Ephrathite of Zereda, Solomon's servant'; 'Ephrathite' here is understood as Ephraimite, so the clue is acceptable.

clues.clue: The prophet Ahijah tore a new garment into twelve pieces and gave me ten.
I became king over the ten northern tribes.
clues.concern: The text says they 'made him king over all Israel', with only Judah following David's house. The 'ten tribes' wording comes from 1 Kings 11:31,35. This is fine.

clues.clue: I set up calves of gold in Beth-el and in Dan.

notes: None of the clues fits Ahab, Omri, or Rehoboam. Ahab and Omri walked in Jeroboam's sins but did not set up the calves. The explanation matches the cited verses.

clues.clue: I was the son of Solomon.
I rejected the counsel of the old men and followed the young men.
I told the people, my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
The ten tribes of Israel rebelled against me.
clues.concern: Minor: 1 Kings 12:19 says Israel rebelled against the house of David. The 'ten tribes' wording comes from 1 Kings 11:31. Fine as a paraphrase of 12:16-20.

notes: The answer is well supported. Jeroboam led the rebellion but was not rebelled against. He was not Solomon's son and did not speak the scorpions line. Abijah and Asa came later. The quoted KJV text and the explanation match 1 Kings 12:14. A parallel account is in 2 Chronicles 10.

clues.clue: A young prophet anointed me king over Israel.
The watchman knew me because I drove furiously.
I had Jezebel thrown down from a window.
clues.concern: Jehu commanded the eunuchs to throw her down (9:32-33), so 'had... thrown down' is accurate.

clues.clue: I destroyed the worship of Baal out of Israel.

notes: All clues are well supported and uniquely fit Jehu. Elisha sent the young prophet but did not anoint Jehu himself. Joram and Ahab fit none of the clues. The explanation quotes 2 Kings 9:20 accurately.

clues.clue: I was a Jew who sat in the king's gate in Shushan.
clues.concern: Esther 2:5 establishes him as a Jew in Shushan the palace; sitting in the king's gate is in Esther 2:19, 2:21. Combined support is fine.

clues.clue: I reported a plot by two chamberlains to kill the king.
clues.concern: Mordecai told Esther, who certified the king in Mordecai's name; 'reported' is acceptable.

clues.clue: I would not bow down to Haman.
I raised my cousin Esther as my own daughter.
clues.concern: KJV calls Esther 'his uncle's daughter' rather than using the word 'cousin', but the meaning is accurate.

notes: Clues clearly identify Mordecai; no distractor fits. Nehemiah was in Shushan but served as cupbearer, not a gate-sitter who refused Haman.

clues.clue: I was a king of the Chaldeans in Babylon.
clues.concern: On its own this also fits Nebuchadnezzar, a Chaldean king of Babylon (Ezra 5:12), but the later clues make the answer clear.

clues.clue: I drank wine from the golden vessels taken from the temple in Jerusalem.
The fingers of a man's hand wrote on the wall of my palace.
I was slain that same night.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 alone could also describe Nebuchadnezzar (Ezra 5:12; Daniel 5:2). The other clues point only to Belshazzar.
notes: The answer and explanation match Daniel 5:30 word for word. Nebuchadnezzar took the vessels (Daniel 5:2), but Belshazzar drank from them, so clue 2 is accurate. Darius received the kingdom afterward (Daniel 5:31) and does not fit the clues.

clues.clue: King Ahasuerus set me above all the princes.
I was full of wrath because a Jew would not bow to me.
clues.concern: Verse 5 does not name Mordecai as a Jew, but Esther 3:4-6 makes it clear. Minor.

clues.clue: I cast Pur, that is, the lot, to choose a day to destroy the Jews.
clues.concern: Esther 3:7 says 'they cast Pur... before Haman.' Esther 9:24 says Haman 'had cast Pur, that is, the lot.' The first-person wording is defensible, but 9:24 is the better support.

clues.clue: I was hanged on the gallows I had prepared for another man.

notes: Haman is the correct and unique answer. Mordecai was later exalted (Esther 10:3), but he was not set above all the princes in the words of Esther 3:1, and none of the other clues fit him. Darius does not appear in Esther. The explanation accurately quotes Esther 7:10.

clues.clue: I was king of Babylon.
clues.concern: Also true of Belshazzar (Daniel 5:1; 7:1 'Belshazzar king of Babylon') and arguably Cyrus (Ezra 5:13 'Cyrus the king of Babylon'); not distinguishing alone, but later clues resolve it.

clues.clue: I dreamed of a great image with a head of gold.
I set up a golden image and commanded everyone to worship it.
clues.concern: The command in Daniel 3:4-6 was to fall down and worship the image, addressed to 'people, nations, and languages'; 'everyone' is a fair paraphrase.

clues.clue: I ate grass as oxen until I knew that the most High rules.
clues.concern: Daniel 4:33 records the eating of grass; the 'until you know that the most High ruleth' purpose clause is in Daniel 4:25 and 4:32, with fulfillment in 4:34-37.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('king of Babylon') also fits Belshazzar (Daniel 5:1; 7:1) and Cyrus (Ezra 5:13). The remaining clues are unique to Nebuchadnezzar, so the item as a whole is unambiguous.
notes: The answer is correct and the explanation accurately reflects Daniel 4:33. Consider making clue 1 more specific (e.g., 'I besieged Jerusalem in the third year of Jehoiakim' – Daniel 1:1) so the first clue does not also fit distractors. Daniel 4:32 might be a better reference label because it contains both the grass-eating and the 'until thou know that the most High ruleth' wording, but 4:33 is acceptable.

clues.clue: I was queen to King Ahasuerus.
clues.concern: This also fits Esther, who became queen to Ahasuerus (Esther 2:17). It does not distinguish Vashti on its own.

clues.clue: I made a feast for the women in the royal house.
I refused to come when the king sent his chamberlains for me.
My royal estate was given to another who was better than I.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('I was queen to King Ahasuerus') also fits Esther (Esther 2:17). Clues 2–4 still uniquely identify Vashti.
notes: The answer is correct, and the explanation matches Esther 1:12. The first clue is non-distinguishing, since Esther was also Ahasuerus's queen. That is acceptable as an opening clue, but it could be sharpened, e.g. 'I was queen to King Ahasuerus before Esther.' The hint is appropriate, since Esther is among the historical books.

clues.clue: I was king of Persia.
clues.concern: Alone, this also fits Darius and Artaxerxes, both called kings of Persia (Ezra 4:24; Ezra 7:1). The later clues resolve it.

clues.clue: The LORD stirred up my spirit to make a proclamation.
I declared that a house should be built for the LORD at Jerusalem.
clues.concern: Darius later confirmed the decree and ordered the work to proceed (Ezra 6:7-12), but the original proclamation to build was Cyrus's (Ezra 6:3). Minor overlap only.

clues.clue: Isaiah calls me the LORD's anointed.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 fits Darius and Artaxerxes, and Darius also decreed support for rebuilding the house (Ezra 6:7-12). Clues 2 and 4 uniquely identify Cyrus.
notes: The explanation is a condensed paraphrase of Ezra 1:2. It omits 'hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth' but is accurate. Isaiah 44:28 also names Cyrus and his role in rebuilding Jerusalem and laying the temple's foundation.

clues.clue: My father was Zebedee.
I was mending nets in a ship when Jesus called me.
clues.concern: Also stated in Mark 1:19. Fine for James. Note that Peter and Andrew were casting a net (Matthew 4:18), not mending nets, so there is no distractor conflict.

clues.clue: Jesus called my brother and me Boanerges, the sons of thunder.
King Herod killed me with the sword.
clues.concern: Acts 12:1 names 'Herod the king' (Herod Agrippa I). This is accurate.

notes: All clues accurately describe James son of Zebedee. None of them fit Peter, Philip, or Andrew. Every clue is unique to James except the father clue, which also applies to John, but John is not an option. The explanation matches Acts 12:2 in the KJV.

clues.clue: I was a blind beggar sitting by the highway near Jericho.
I cried out, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.
When many told me to be quiet, I cried all the more.
clues.concern: KJV wording is 'many charged him that he should hold his peace: but he cried the more a great deal'; the paraphrase is accurate.

clues.clue: I cast away my garment, came to Jesus and received my sight.

notes: All clues match Mark 10:46-52. Distractors do not fit. Lazarus the beggar (Luke 16:20) was not blind, and Zacchaeus, though at Jericho, was not blind. Parallel accounts in Matthew 20:30 (two blind men) and Luke 18:35 (unnamed) do not name the man, so Bartimaeus is uniquely correct.

clues.clue: My sister was Martha and my brother was Lazarus.
I sat at Jesus' feet and heard his word.
Jesus said I had chosen that good part.
I anointed Jesus' feet with costly spikenard and wiped them with my hair.
clues.concern: This is accurate for John 12:3, but the details come from John, not Luke. The hint 'Look in Luke' covers only clues 2-3.

notes: The answer is correct. Martha is excluded because she is the sister named in clue 1, and Mary Magdalene and Salome fit none of the clues. The explanation accurately paraphrases Luke 10:39. The hint 'Look in Luke' is partially incomplete, since clues 1 and 4 are drawn from John 11-12.

clues.clue: I was a prisoner in Jerusalem.
clues.concern: Matthew 27:16 calls him 'a notable prisoner'. Jerusalem is not named in the verse, but it is implied by the trial setting before Pilate.

clues.clue: I had been bound with others who had made insurrection and committed murder.
Pilate offered the crowd a choice between Jesus and me.
The people asked for me to be released.

notes: The answer, Barabbas, is correct and the explanation accurately quotes Mark 15:15. None of the distractors fit the clues.

clues.clue: I was a ruler of the synagogue.
clues.concern: Mark says 'one of the rulers of the synagogue'; Luke 8:41 says 'a ruler of the synagogue'. Nicodemus was 'a ruler of the Jews' (John 3:1), not of a synagogue, so there is no real conflict, but it is a slight surface overlap.

clues.clue: I fell at Jesus' feet and begged him to come to my house.
My twelve-year-old daughter was dying.
clues.concern: Luke says 'about twelve years of age'. Mark 5:42 gives her age only after the miracle.

clues.clue: Jesus took her by the hand and said, Talitha cumi.
clues.concern: By this point she had died (Mark 5:35, 5:39). The clue is accurate but reads as a raising from death, not a healing of a dying girl.

notes: The item is accurate. The explanation matches Mark 5:22 in the KJV. The 'begged him to come to my house' wording fits Luke 8:41 best; Mark 5:23 says 'come and lay thy hands on her'.

clues.clue: I was coming into Jerusalem out of the country.
clues.concern: The text says only 'coming out of the country' (also Luke 23:26). 'Into Jerusalem' is a reasonable contextual inference, since the crucifixion procession left the city, but it is not stated explicitly.

clues.clue: Soldiers compelled me to carry a cross.
clues.concern: The verse says 'they compelled'. That 'they' were soldiers comes from context (Matthew 27:27; Mark 15:16). This is acceptable.

clues.clue: The cross I carried was the cross of Jesus.
I came from Cyrene and was the father of Alexander and Rufus.

notes: The answer is correct and well supported by Mark 15:21, with parallels in Matthew 27:32 and Luke 23:26. The explanation accurately paraphrases the cited verse. One minor point: the phrase 'into Jerusalem' in clue 1 is inferred rather than quoted from the text. No distractor fits any of the clues.

clues.clue: I was an honourable counsellor who waited for the kingdom of God.
clues.concern: Not in Matthew; Luke 23:50-51 also calls him 'a counsellor' who 'waited for the kingdom of God'. Nicodemus was also a council member ('a ruler of the Jews', John 3:1; 'being one of them', John 7:50), but the exact wording fits only Joseph.

clues.clue: I was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly, for fear of the Jews.
clues.concern: Only John records the secrecy. Nicodemus came to Jesus by night (John 3:2; 19:39), so a player might link secrecy to him, but the 'secret disciple for fear of the Jews' wording applies to Joseph.

clues.clue: I went in boldly to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
clues.concern: 'Boldly' comes from Mark only; Matthew 27:58 says simply that he 'went to Pilate, and begged the body'.

clues.clue: I laid Jesus in my own new tomb, hewn out in the rock.
clues.concern: Nicodemus helped with the burial (John 19:39-40), but the tomb was Joseph's own, so this clue is distinctive.

notes: The answer and explanation match Matthew 27:59-60 accurately. The hint 'Look in Matthew' is only partly helpful: clue 1 comes from Mark and Luke, clue 2 from John, and clue 3's 'boldly' from Mark. Consider broadening the hint to 'Look in the Gospels' or noting that the clues draw on all four accounts. Nicodemus is a strong but defensible distractor: no clue fits him exactly, though he shares council membership, a measure of secrecy, and a role in the burial.

clues.clue: I was a disciple living in Damascus.
The Lord spoke to me in a vision about a man named Saul.
I was afraid, because I had heard how much evil Saul had done.
clues.concern: The KJV does not say Ananias was 'afraid.' It records only his objection: 'I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints at Jerusalem.' Fear is a reasonable inference, not a stated fact. Better wording: 'I told the Lord I had heard how much evil Saul had done to his saints.'

clues.clue: I put my hands on Saul so that he might receive his sight.

notes: Ananias is the correct answer, and none of the distractors fits the clue set. In Acts 9:26 it is the Jerusalem disciples, not Barnabas, who were afraid of Saul, so clue 3 does not really point to Barnabas. The explanation accurately paraphrases Acts 9:17. Suggest rewording clue 3 to match the text more closely.

clues.clue: I was a king who came to Caesarea with Bernice to greet Festus.
Festus told me about a prisoner named Paul.
Paul made his defence before me.
clues.concern: Paul also made defences before Felix (Acts 24:10) and Festus (Acts 25:8), so this clue alone fits distractors. The other clues still make the answer unique.

clues.clue: I said to Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.

distractor_conflict: Clue 3 ('Paul made his defence before me') also fits Felix (Acts 24:10) and Festus (Acts 25:8). The other clues uniquely identify Agrippa, so this is not disqualifying.
notes: The item is accurate overall. Clue 3 could be sharpened, for example: 'Paul said he thought himself happy to answer for himself before me' (Acts 26:2). Difficulty 4 seems high, since clue 4 is a famous line.

clues.clue: I was a young man in Troas.
clues.concern: Troas is established in Acts 20:6, and 'young man' comes from Acts 20:9. The text does not say Eutychus lived in Troas, only that he was there. Timothy and Tychicus were also at Troas (Acts 20:4-5), and Timothy is called young (1 Timothy 4:12), so this clue alone does not single out Eutychus. The later clues do.

clues.clue: I sat in a window while Paul preached until midnight.
clues.concern: The window is in verse 9 and 'continued his speech until midnight' is in verse 7. This is accurate.

clues.clue: I fell into a deep sleep and fell down from the third loft.
Paul embraced me, and I was brought alive.
clues.concern: 'Embracing him' is in verse 10, and 'they brought the young man alive' is in verse 12. This is accurate.

distractor_conflict: Only weakly: clue 1 ('young man in Troas') could loosely fit Timothy, who was at Troas (Acts 20:4-5) and young (1 Timothy 4:12). Tychicus was also at Troas. The remaining clues are unique to Eutychus.
notes: The answer is correct and the explanation matches Acts 20:9. Consider citing Acts 20:9-12 as the reference label, since clue 4 depends on verses 10-12. Clue 1 could be tightened, for example to 'a young man who listened to Paul at Troas.'

clues.clue: I followed Jesus from the baptism of John until he was taken up.
clues.concern: This is the stated qualification for the candidates, not a direct statement about Matthias. It is implied by his being appointed (Acts 1:23), so it is acceptable.

clues.clue: My name was put forward together with Joseph called Barsabas.
The apostles prayed and gave forth their lots.
clues.concern: KJV says only 'they prayed'. The group present was about 120 disciples (Acts 1:15), so attributing the prayer specifically to 'the apostles' slightly overstates the text. The clue also describes the group's action rather than the speaker's, so it adds little identifying value.

clues.clue: I was numbered with the eleven apostles in the place of Judas.
clues.concern: 'In the place of Judas' is drawn from Acts 1:25 ('from which Judas by transgression fell'), combined with verse 26. This is accurate.

notes: Matthias is the correct answer, and the explanation matches the KJV wording of Acts 1:26. None of the clues fits Barnabas, Stephen, or Silas. Players could confuse 'Joseph called Barsabas' (Acts 1:23) with 'Joses... surnamed Barnabas' (Acts 4:36), but clue 2 names Barsabas as the other candidate, so there is no real conflict. Consider rewording clue 3 to 'They prayed and gave forth their lots, and the lot fell upon me.' That would be more faithful to the text and more identifying.

clues.clue: Many gathered to pray at my mother Mary's house in Jerusalem.
I went with Barnabas and Saul but left them in Pamphylia.
clues.concern: Acts 13:13 says John departed from them at Perga in Pamphylia and returned to Jerusalem, and Acts 15:38 says he departed from them from Pamphylia. Acts 12:25 and 13:5 show him going with Barnabas and Saul. The clue is accurate.

clues.clue: Paul and Barnabas parted over whether to take me again.
Paul later wrote that I was profitable to him for the ministry.

notes: All clues fit John Mark. None of the clues fits Luke, Timothy or Silas. Silas replaced Mark as Paul's companion (Acts 15:40) but was not the subject of the dispute. The explanation accurately reflects Acts 15:39.

clues.clue: I departed from my master for a season.
clues.concern: The verse says 'he therefore departed for a season'; 'from my master' is implied by context rather than stated, but it is a fair reading.

clues.clue: Paul begat me in the faith while he was in bonds.
clues.concern: KJV says 'begotten in my bonds'; 'in the faith' is an interpretive addition. Titus is also called Paul's 'own son after the common faith' (Titus 1:4), but not in connection with bonds, so the clue still distinguishes Onesimus.

clues.clue: I was once unprofitable to my master, but now profitable.
Paul sent me back to Philemon as a brother beloved.
clues.concern: Combines v.12 ('whom I have sent again') with v.16 ('a brother beloved'). There is minor overlap with Tychicus, who is called 'a beloved brother' and was sent to Colossae with Onesimus (Colossians 4:7-9). However, Tychicus was not sent back to Philemon as a returning servant, so the overlap is slight.

notes: The answer, Onesimus, is clearly correct, and the explanation quotes Philemon 1:10 accurately. The slight phrasing liberties ('in the faith', 'from my master') are acceptable paraphrases. Overlap with the Tychicus option ('beloved brother', Colossians 4:7) is minimal because the clues are specific to Philemon.
